blocks.text: In which of the following regions of India are shale gas resources found?

1. Cambay Basin
2. Cauvery Basin
3. Krishna-Godavari Basin
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

sourceTitle: UPSC CSE 2016 General Studies Paper I · Series A

explanation.justification: Oil Shales are usually fine-grained sedimentary rocks containing relatively large amounts of organic matter from which significant quantities of shale oil and combustible gas can be extracted by destructive distillation. Shale gas can emerge as an important new source of energy in the country. India has several Shale Formations which seem to hold shale gas. The Shale Gas Formations are spread over several sedimentary basins, such as, Gangetic plain, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and other coastal areas in the country including hydrocarbon-bearing ones Cambay, Assam Arkan & Damodar Basins have large shale deposits. Various developmental activities are going on in Gandhar area of Cambay Basin, Krishna-Godavari Basin, Cauvery Basin and Assam & Assam Arkan Basin. ONGC is presently carrying out shale gas and oil exploration in four onland basins, namely, Cambay, KG, Cauvery, Assam and Assam-Arakan. A total of twelve exploratory locations for shale gas and oil are available for drilling in 2016-17 and subsequent year. In addition, coring and other data collection are planned in suitable exploratory wells in identified blocks. ONGC has drilled 18 wells so far and one well is under drilling. So far 69 cores have been collected in 17 wells.

1. Carbon dioxide
2. Carbon monoxide
3. Nitrogen dioxide
4. Sulfur dioxide
5. Methane
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

sourceTitle: UPSC CSE 2016 General Studies Paper I · Series A

explanation.justification: The National Air Quality Index (AQI) in India is calculated based on eight primary pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, Nitrogen Dioxide ($NO_2$), Sulfur Dioxide ($SO_2$), Carbon Monoxide (CO), Ozone ($O_3$), Ammonia ($NH_3$), and Lead (Pb).  It does not include Carbon dioxide or Methane, which are global warming gases rather than direct local air quality pollutants.

question:
With reference to 'Astrosat', the astronomical observatory launched by India, which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. Other than USA and Russia, India is the only country to have launched a similar observatory into space.
2. Astrosat is a 2000 kg satellite placed in an orbit at 1650 km above the surface of the Earth.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

blocks.text: With reference to 'Astrosat', the astronomical observatory launched by India, which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. Other than USA and Russia, India is the only country to have launched a similar observatory into space.
2. Astrosat is a 2000 kg satellite placed in an orbit at 1650 km above the surface of the Earth.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

sourceTitle: UPSC CSE 2016 General Studies Paper I · Series A

explanation.justification: India is not the only country; Japan and Europe have also launched similar space observatories (Statement 1 is incorrect). Astrosat has a lift-off mass of 1515 kg (not 2000 kg) and is placed in a 650 km orbit (not 1650 km) (Statement 2 is incorrect).

explanation.justification: The memorizing of chronicles, dynastic histories, or epic tales was the specialized work of a group of people known as the sutas and magadhas. question:
With reference to the Agreement at the UNFCCC Meeting in Paris in 2015, which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. The Agreement was signed by all the member countries of the UN and it will go into effect in 2017.
2. The Agreement aims to limit the greenhouse gas emissions so that the rise in average global temperature by the end of this century does not exceed 2 °C or even 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels.
3. Developed countries acknowledged their historical responsibility in global warming and committed to donate $ 1000 billion a year from 2020 to help developing countries to cope with climate change.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

blocks.text: With reference to the Agreement at the UNFCCC Meeting in Paris in 2015, which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. The Agreement was signed by all the member countries of the UN and it will go into effect in 2017.
2. The Agreement aims to limit the greenhouse gas emissions so that the rise in average global temperature by the end of this century does not exceed 2 °C or even 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels.
3. Developed countries acknowledged their historical responsibility in global warming and committed to donate $ 1000 billion a year from 2020 to help developing countries to cope with climate change.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

sourceTitle: UPSC CSE 2016 General Studies Paper I · Series A

explanation.justification: The Paris Agreement aims to limit global temperature rise to well below 2°C, preferably to $1.5^{\circ}C$ (Statement 2 is correct).  Not all UN members signed it initially, and its major climate action targets were intended to start post-2020, not 2017 (Statement 1 is incorrect).  The climate finance commitment by developed countries was $100 billion per year, not $1000 billion (Statement 3 is incorrect).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

blocks.text: Consider the following statements:

2. The Sustainable Development Goals have to be achieved by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

sourceTitle: UPSC CSE 2016 General Studies Paper I · Series A

explanation.justification: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were set up in 2015 by the United Nations General Assembly, not the Club of Rome in 1972 (Statement 1 is incorrect).  The 17 interlinked global goals are intended to be achieved by the year 2030 (Statement 2 is correct).
